prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 4.32. Exact Sanskrit: एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥ ३२ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Thus many kinds of sacrifices are spread out in the mouth of Brahman (the Vedas). Know them all to be born from action; knowing this thus, you shall be liberated. Chapter context: Knowledge, action, teaching lineage, offering and insight. Depict the verse-specific symbolism; the iconic divine descent is appropriate only where stated. Distinguish the many kinds of offering without text labels. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Those who eat the nectar-like remnant of sacrifice go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not (joyful) for one who performs no sacrifice, O best of Kurus — how then the next world? Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Superior to the sacrifice made of material wealth is the sacrifice of knowledge, O Parantapa. All action in its entirety, O Pārtha, reaches its culmination and fulfillment in knowledge. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 4.32: Thus many kinds of sacrifices are spread out in the mouth of Brahman (the Vedas). Know them all to be born from action; knowing this thus, you shall be liberated.
